nodes.label: map vs fold and domain fast-path findings
nodes.norm_label: map vs fold and domain fast-path findings
nodes.rationale: Comparing map with threaded fold for application updates found that avoiding unnecessary reflection arithmetic mattered much more than changing the combinator; an idiom audit should question the algorithm's work, not just its control shape.

nodes.label: Durable Result Metadata Requirements
nodes.rationale: Durable experiments must record commits, OS/CPU, power state, compiler, build config, and paired ratios so results remain attributable and reproducible.

nodes.label: Predicate Observer Rule
nodes.rationale: Combinators running a predicate restore the surrounding data stack after reading its boolean result; side effects are not undone; only try owns recoverable stack restoration.

nodes.label: dip private error-cleanup snapshot ownership cliff
nodes.norm_label: dip private error-cleanup snapshot ownership cliff
nodes.rationale: Comparing direct vs dip-based BFS layouts exposed that dip retained a private error-cleanup snapshot, forcing copies of the ambient state each iteration; removing the snapshot made BFS layouts linear.

nodes.label: Stack/Capture Division of State
nodes.rationale: The stack carries changing algorithm state (deque, set, vector, pqueue); captures name only stable context and scalars. This avoids accidental snapshot retention through copies of evolving collections.

nodes.label: Captures Name Context, Not Mutable Variables
nodes.norm_label: captures name context, not mutable variables
nodes.rationale: Capturing an evolving collection causes copy-on-write copies on each update because every fetch shares the captured value; fold threading keeps a single reference and is linear.

nodes.label: Route Aggregation via fold and captures
nodes.norm_label: route aggregation via fold and captures
nodes.rationale: The growing route map is threaded through fold while captures name only the fixed-size previous group and stable input fields, preventing repeated copies of the growing map.

nodes.label: Paired Comparison Methodology
nodes.rationale: Paired candidate/baseline ratios with alternating order and warmups are the primary result because they are less sensitive to temperature, CPU frequency, and background activity than unpaired samples.

nodes.label: map/times Population Update Pattern
nodes.rationale: map expresses one new record per particle; times threads the evolving population while timestep and gravity stay in stable captures; gravity delta is computed once at the entry point rather than per particle.

nodes.label: Stop retaining ambient stack for private error cleanup
nodes.norm_label: stop retaining ambient stack for private error cleanup
nodes.rationale: State-threading combinators were retaining the ambient stack solely for private error cleanup, forcing copy-on-write copies on every ambient update; removing that retention restores linear state-threaded updates.

nodes.label: Repository Invariants
nodes.rationale: builtins.json is canonical builtin metadata; native words must schedule frames rather than re-enter tf_vm_exec(); runtime code must retain/release object references; SDK releases must be self-contained.

nodes.label: Iterative VM Frame Stack
nodes.rationale: Toy calls do not recurse through the C call stack; the runtime records pending work in an explicit frame stack processed by the main VM loop, so native words must schedule frames instead of re-entering execution.

nodes.label: Symbol vs Call Distinction
nodes.rationale: Names are data; call instructions run words. The conversion is explicit (>symbol, >call) so moving names never accidentally executes code; call instructions are deliberately not hashable.

nodes.label: Directory-as-Package Model
nodes.rationale: The directory is the unit of loading and namespacing; files only split its implementation, so filename order has no semantic effect and declarations are collected before any word body runs.

nodes.label: Deferred Call API (toy_defer_call)
nodes.rationale: Fire-and-forget FIFO queue lets C callbacks notify Toy without recursively entering the VM, preserving the iterative execution model; result-bearing continuations are deferred.

nodes.label: Rejected synchronized global-pool candidate
nodes.rationale: Synchronizing process-wide object and list pools was correct but too slow (+56.7% list workload, +388.5% concat), so per-state pools were adopted instead to allow concurrent independent states without contention.

nodes.label: Typed Resource Values
nodes.rationale: External handles are wrapped with a copied type tag and exactly-once destructor; the foreign pointer is never exposed to Toy code.

nodes.label: Four rejected call-path runtime prototypes
nodes.rationale: Frame ownership, quotation-cache acquisition, prepared user-word calls, and initial conditional scheduling were each tested; none produced dependable application improvement, so an isolated call-loop win or counter reduction is not sufficient evidence of an application gain.

nodes.label: Dispatch change rejection on noisy timings
nodes.norm_label: dispatch change rejection on noisy timings
nodes.rationale: Two dispatch micro-optimizations produced inconsistent swings across pairs on a noisy machine and were discarded; future dispatch work should start from a more controlled profile or benchmark environment rather than timing alone.
